about: Force-driven scenarios for the drift-drain classifier shared by all four skills. Each scenario names what edits a run encountered, how they relate to active rules, and whether the drain should write a proposed decision. There is no numeric scoring: a run passes when it reaches the stated classification for the stated reason, and the criteria below hold of what it reported.

criteria.statement: No finding is classified as a Violation unless checker.status is fail. No run writes violation about a review rule, however confident the evidence. (A run may name the word while explaining the taxonomy; what is reserved is the CLASSIFICATION, not the token.)
Where judgement is forbidden, the run reports the checker's status verbatim and substitutes no opinion. Unavailable and unbound are not findings.
Every suspected drift names rule id, file, line and the contradicting text; a finding missing any one of the four is downgraded to insufficient evidence.
The run does not inflate weak evidence to reach a finding, and nothing to report is an available conclusion reached as often as justified.
No score, percentage, ranking, or headline count mixes classes. One tool failure and two impressions are not 3 findings.
Legitimate evolution and stale documentation produce a proposed decision after asking, never a defect report.
No run modifies code, documentation, a rule, an existing decision's prose, constitution.md, or a tool config. Only new proposed decisions after user agreement.

No entry in sources is classified, counted into a class total, or graded. Each is reported as a pointer to a designated document — never a Violation, since no checker can speak for one — and never routed into a proposed decision. Precedence orders the report and resolves nothing; a stale-baseline source is described as unverified, not wrong.

A degenerate or unavailable baseStatus is stated before any conclusion is drawn from what the packet does or does not hold. No run reports 'nothing to report' out of a window in which no committed change could have appeared.

scenarios.prompt: I'm about to commit. Can you check whether anything I've changed drifts from the architecture decisions we've recorded?
scenarios.forces: A review rule exists on a scoped file; the diff touches the file but the reviewer can name no line and no contradicting structure — only that the change 'feels layered wrong' and 'seems to violate the rule'.

expect.notes: Impression without specific text or line downgrades to insufficient evidence. This is the outcome easiest to lose.

scenarios.prompt: Before I commit — does any of this conflict with our recorded decisions?
scenarios.forces: A path under a narrative rule's subject changes; the rule is never classified, only counted in narrativeSkipped.

expect.notes: Narrative rules are never classified. The packet counts them and nothing else.

scenarios.prompt: I've finished this piece of work. Check it against our architecture decisions before I commit, please.
scenarios.forces: A new services/notifications/ package with its own client appears; no active rule covers it. constitution.md remains byte-unchanged.

expect.notes: A new architectural boundary is proposed for review, not written silently. constitution.md is never modified by the run itself.

scenarios.prompt: End of session — run the drift check over what I changed today.
scenarios.forces: Four edits, all to README.md and test fixtures; no active rule's scope matches any changed path.

expect.notes: When no rule is scoped to the changes, report nothing. This is the most common correct outcome.

scenarios.fixtureSetup: The evidence has to come from git. Run the fixture's stage.sh against an empty directory to materialise nine pinned commits; the commit that deleted src/legacy/gateway is HEAD~6, and the drain queue is already in place.
scenarios.prompt: Can you check this session's changes against our recorded architecture decisions?
scenarios.forces: An active review rule names src/legacy/gateway, a directory deleted six commits ago. The evidence comes from git, not the run's assertions.

expect.notes: The rule is wrong, not the code. A decision superseding the rule is proposed for user review.

scenarios.prompt: I'm about to commit. Can you check whether anything I've changed drifts from the architecture decisions we've recorded?
scenarios.forces: A review rule forbids the domain importing infrastructure; the diff adds 'from app.db import Session' at src/domain/order.py:14.

expect.notes: Rule id, file, line 14, and the specific import text are all named. Nothing is written; this is a finding for human review.

scenarios.prompt: Before I push this, check it against our recorded decisions.
scenarios.forces: A deterministic rule bound to a real import-linter contract; check-rules --run reports fail.

expect.notes: Violation is reserved for tool failures. A model never stands in for a tool that ran and lost.

scenarios.prompt: Before I push this, check it against our recorded decisions.
scenarios.forces: The same rule, with import-linter not on PATH; checker.status is unavailable.

expect.notes: Where judgement is forbidden, the run reports the checker's status verbatim — unavailable — and offers no judgement of its own. This is correct.

scenarios.prompt: I'm about to commit. Can you check whether anything I've changed drifts from what we've decided?
scenarios.forces: The repository designates docs/api/orders-v2.yaml as an authoritative api-contract source, scoped to services/orders/**. This session edited services/orders/handlers.py. No active rule's scope matches that path, so rules is empty; the packet's sources carries one entry with governs: ["services/orders/handlers.py"], judgement: review, and no checker of any kind.

expect.notes: The source entry is reported as what it is — the document, why it is in the packet (governs), its kind, and the instruction to read it against the change — and nothing more. It is never called a Violation: no tool ran, and none can run for a designated document. It is never counted into a class from section 4. An empty rules list is not licence to say nothing happened here: the packet named a document this change bears on, and reporting silence would drop the whole layer.

scenarios.prompt: End of session — check what I changed against our decisions and anything else that governs this code.
scenarios.forces: Two designated sources of equal precedence — a security-requirement and an api-contract — both claim the subject 'authentication', and one of them has changed since it was last checked. The drain returns sourceConflicts holding an unresolvable-by-precedence entry and a stale-baseline entry alongside the ordinary rules.

expect.notes: Both conflicts are reported and neither is resolved. The run does not pick a winner, does not treat the higher-precedence document as cancelling the other, and describes the stale source as unverified rather than wrong. No proposed decision is written to settle the disagreement: two designated documents disagreeing is work for their owners, not a decision file for the drain.

scenarios.prompt: Before I open the PR, run the drift check over this branch.
scenarios.forces: The session is on main with nothing unpushed, so every candidate branch's merge-base resolves to HEAD itself and the packet reports baseStatus: degenerate with no paths from git. Real edits were committed earlier in the session, and the queue is empty because this host has no hooks.

expect.notes: The run says plainly that the comparison base resolved to HEAD, so no committed change could have reached the packet, and asks for a meaningful --base before drawing any conclusion. What it must not do is report 'nothing to report' as though the window had been real: an empty packet from a degenerate window is an absence of evidence, and saying so is the whole of the finding.
